item.title: 9 compact portable coffee makers for a reliable caffeine hit wherever you go
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
For caffeine addicts, a dedicated coffee machine is a worthy investment. But that's very much an at-home setup — what about when you're out and about? Sometimes, a great local coffee shop will satisfy your cravings, but that's no given. If you're serious about your caffeine hit, best to arm yourself with a sturdy, portable coffee maker that leaves nothing to chance. There are a handful of brands that dominate in this market. One is AeroPress, which shot to popularity with its innovative design that aims to combine the best bits of French press, pour-over, and espresso brewing. The original model's compact, plastic build makes it pretty travel-friendly, but now there's also a smaller 'Go' version with an integrated travel cup and filter-paper holder. Wacaco makes a range of sturdy, hand-powered brewers that deliver an espresso with a rich crema. You release a front button and then press it in to extract the coffee — your squeezes turn into 18 bars (261 PSI) of stable pressure inside the capsule. Don't have the means to boil water up separately? The OutIn does the heating part for you. It's USB-C rechargeable and works with capsules or ground coffee. This one's also great if the manual part poses a problem for you: it starts brewing at the press of a button, with no pushing or squeezing required. (Dreame has a similar self-heating portable machine on the way, but it's not on sale yet.) One final system it's worth drawing attention to is the Rok Presso. This looks a little bit like a two-armed corkscrew, although it's rather bigger in real life. You add ground coffee, press down on the arms, and rather than pulling up a cork, the mechanism below produces a shot of espresso. It's not the most portable option here, but as a power-free, streamlined alternative to a traditional machine it's intriguing. Many designs also incorporate built-in RFID-blocking technology to safeguard your cards against fraud while abroad, while others include dedicated slots for luggage trackers like Apple AirTags for added security. Currently the special offer knocks it down to the same price as the lower Standard plan at just $2.49 per month, and you’ll receive three extra months at sign-up. What is the best VPN deal? Right now, the 2-year plan for NordVPN‘s Complete tier is the best deal. Included with this Plus tier are advanced protections such as a password manager and threat protection, plus 1TB of cloud storage. When’s the best time to shop for a VPN? Typically you’ll want to time your VPN shopping around a prominent sales period. The biggest sales periods are Black Friday/Cyber Monday in late November . The best sales often occur leading up to and during these two events and they are great times to snag a VPN subscription for cheap. Many VPN providers have even begun extending these deals past Cyber Monday and through to the end of the year. What should I look for in a VPN deal? There are a few things you should keep in mind when shopping for a good VPN deal. The first thing to consider is, of course, your budget. How much are you willing to spend each month? How much can you afford to drop on a longer-term plan with an upfront payment? You’ll also need to determine how long you intend to use the VPN. Do you just need it for a short trip? A few months? Or forever? The very best VPN deals are generally on longer-term plans for two or three years. After you decide on your budget and how long you’ll use the VPN, next you can start comparing features. Look at the number of servers and locations for each VPN. A good starting point is to look for services that have at least 1,000 servers and 30 or more country locations. The next thing to consider is VPN speed. This may be tricky to do since you aren’t likely to be able to test connection speeds without first paying to use the service. Look for reviews, like ours, that give you a relative average of connection speeds rather than direct Mbps speed comparisons for a more accurate picture. Finally, compare each VPN’s privacy protections. Does it have a no-logs policy? Has it undergone any independent audits of its servers? Where is the VPN company located? You connect to a VPN server, which can be located in the United States or a foreign country (like France or Japan). Your web traffic then goes through that server to make it appear as though you’re browsing from that server’s location and not from your actual location. When you’re using a VPN, it’s difficult for others to snoop on your web-browsing activity. Only you, the VPN service, and the website you’re visiting will know what you’re up to. A VPN can be a great solution to a variety of concerns, such as online privacy, anonymity, greater security on public Wi-Fi, and, of course, spoofing locations.

item.title: Highest-ever offers ending soon: Earn up to 125,000 miles with Citi / AAdvantage cards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy
Highest-ever offers ending soon: Earn up to 125,000 miles with Citi / AAdvantage cards If you are a frequent American Airlines flyer, you have plenty of credit card options to help you earn additional miles and make the most of every American Airlines flight. For a limited time, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is offering its highest-ever welcome offer, along with new card benefits and perks as part of the card's refresh in August. Meanwhile, for a limited time, new Citi® / AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard® (see rates and fees) cardholders can earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $3,500 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. This matches the highest offer we've seen on the card. The offers on the Citi / AAdvantage Executive and Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select are ending soon, so don't wait if you have been eyeing either card. Here's a rundown of the top Citi / AAdvantage credit cards and their current offers. Holding one of these cards could be a straightforward way to score a business-class ticket on American or one of its Oneworld partners. Comparison of the Citi / AAdvantage welcome offers *The offer value is based on TPG's October 2026 valuations. The information for the Citi / AAdvantage Business World Elite Mastercard and AAdvantage MileUp card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. The Citi / AA Executive is American's top-tier personal card. Best for: Those who want Admirals Club access Welcome bonus: For a limited time, earn 125,000 bonus miles after spending $15,000 on purchases in the first five months from account opening. Offer ends soon. According to TPG's valuations, the welcome bonus is worth $1,813. This is the highest welcome offer we've seen in the card's history, so if you are interested, now is the best time to apply. Earning rates: - 12 miles per dollar spent on eligible car rentals and hotels booked through American's car rental and hotel booking sites, respectively - 4 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases - 1 mile per dollar spent on all other purchases This card is best suited to frequent American Airlines flyers who can take advantage of its Admirals Club membership, statement credits and elite-status benefits. At $695, the Citi / AAdvantage Executive has a much higher annual fee than other options but comes with a notable benefit for frequent flyers: Admirals Club access for you and up to two guests traveling with you (when you have a same-day boarding pass for an eligible flight). Cardholders also receive: - Up to $500 credit annually toward eligible American Airlines Vacations purchases (up to $250 from Jan. 1 through June 30 and up to $250 from July 1 through Dec. 31) - Up to $100 credit annually toward eligible inflight and Admirals Club purchases - Complimentary Omni Hotels & Resorts Champion status (enrollment required) and an annual Omni free night reward after a qualifying stay† - Avis President's club status (enrollment available through Aug. 31, 2028) †A qualifying stay is one of two or more consecutive nights booked directly through Omni Hotels and Resorts on omnihotels.com. Enrollment in the Champion Status benefit is required. The card also offers travel protections and the ability to earn up to 40,000 bonus Loyalty Points per elite qualification period, making it particularly useful for those pursuing American elite status. The Citi / AA Business is Citi's business card for American Airlines loyalists. Welcome bonus: Earn 65,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. According to TPG's valuations, the welcome bonus is worth $943. This is the standard offer we see in the card's history, so we'd recommend waiting for a better offer if you can. Annual fee: $0 introductory annual fee for the first 12 months, then $99 thereafter - 2 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases and eligible business expenses, including cable and satellite providers, car rentals, gas stations and telecommunications merchants - 1 mile per dollar spent on everything else With this card, you and up to four companions get a free first checked bag when flying a domestic American Airlines itinerary on the same reservation. If you spend $30,000 with the card in a cardholder year and renew your card, you'll earn a companion certificate, which allows you to take a companion on a flight for $99 (plus taxes and fees). The certificate can only be used for a round-trip, domestic itinerary (i.e., one to and from the 48 contiguous states, unless you live in Alaska or Hawaii) in the Main Cabin. The certificate is granted upon account renewal, and the account must remain open for a full billing cycle after the anniversary date. The Citi / AA Globe is best suited for those who fly often but not enough to justify having the premium card. Best for: Semifrequent American Airlines flyers Welcome bonus: Earn 60,000 bonus miles after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. According to TPG's valuations, the welcome bonus is worth $870. This is the standard offer on the card, so we recommend waiting to apply. - 6 miles per dollar spent on eligible AAdvantage Hotels bookings - 3 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases - 2 miles per dollar spent at restaurants, including takeout and delivery, and on eligible "Rides and Rails" purchases, including taxis, ride-hailing services and public transit The Globe's standout perks include four Admirals Club passes each calendar year and a 5,000 "Flight Streak" Loyalty Point boost after four eligible American Airlines flights. You can do this up to three times per year for a total of 15,000 Loyalty Points. The card also provides an annual companion certificate each cardholder year, allowing you to pay $99 (plus taxes and fees) for a round-trip domestic Main Cabin ticket each year. Plus, you'll receive the first checked bag free for the cardholder and up to eight companions on the same reservation, preferred boarding and a Splurge credit. It's a decent option for those who can take advantage of the card's companion certificate, lounge access and AAdvantage-related perks in exchange for a more modest $350 annual fee. The Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select is a solid option for American Airlines flyers who want basic airline perks without paying for a more premium card. Best for: Casual American Airlines flyers Welcome bonus: For a limited time, earn 80,000 bonus miles after spending $3,500 on purchases in the first four months from account opening. Offer ends soon. According to TPG's valuations, the welcome bonus is worth $1,160. This matches the highest offer we've seen on the card, so now is a great time to apply. - 2 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases, plus gas station and restaurant purchases If you fly American Airlines often enough to want an upgraded flight experience but are uninterested in Admirals Club access, this is a solid card option. It's affordable and easy to keep in your wallet. You'll receive benefits like preferred boarding, a free first checked bag for you and up to four companions on domestic American Airlines itineraries, and discounts on inflight snacks and beverage purchases. As a cardholder, you'll also earn 1 Loyalty Point for every eligible AAdvantage mile earned from purchases, and this card does not charge foreign transaction fees. Another great benefit of this card is the ability to earn a $125 American Airlines flight discount after spending $20,000 or more on purchases during your card membership year and renewing your card. The Citi / AA MileUp is Citi's entry-level American Airlines product. Welcome bonus: Earn 15,000 bonus miles and a $100 statement credit after spending $500 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. According to TPG's valuations, this welcome bonus is worth $318 (including the statement credit). This is the standard offer we typically see in the card's history. Best for: Beginners looking to earn American Airlines miles - 2 miles per dollar spent on eligible American Airlines purchases and at grocery stores, including grocery delivery services If you're a beginner looking for an inexpensive way to earn American miles, this could be a good entry point into the Citi AAdvantage credit card lineup. As a no-annual-fee card, it offers few perks, but you will get 25% savings on inflight drinks and snacks. However, anyone taking more than a couple of American Airlines flights per year will likely be better off with an American Airlines card that charges an annual fee, since those cards offer higher earning rates and more valuable perks. Citi doesn't limit the total number of credit cards you can hold, but it does cap your overall credit line across accounts. You can only apply for one card every eight days, no more than two cards in 65 days and just one business card every 90 days. Finally, Citi's 48-month rule means you can't earn a welcome bonus on the same AAdvantage card if you've received that bonus within the past four years. If you're an American Airlines loyalist, a Citi / AAdvantage credit card can deliver useful benefits, from free checked bags and preferred boarding to bonus miles that can help you book your next award flight. Right now, two cards stand out for their welcome offers: The Citi / AA Executive is offering its highest-ever bonus, while the Citi / AAdvantage Platinum Select is matching the highest offer we've seen on the card. With both limited-time offers ending soon, now is a good time to consider applying if either card fits your travel needs. Whether you're after entry-level earning, mid-tier perks or premium Admirals Club access, there's a Citi / AAdvantage card for a range of American Airlines flyers.

The best thing about Nashville is that everybody sings to their own tune. Itâs a town of creatives. The best boutique hotels in Nashville reflect that creative chaos. Many of the properties are so distinct, itâs hard to believe they share the same zip code. While each of the intimate hotels on this list is completely different, they all provide an authentic Nashville experience, whether you're looking to be blocks from Broadway or in a suburb where you can live like a local. Here are the nine boutique hotels in Nashville I recommend to my friends and family when they come to town. FAQ: What is the difference between a hotel and a boutique hotel? Boutique hotels are a category of hotel. They typically have fewer than 100 guest rooms and offer a one-of-a-kind vibe that makes the property stand out. They are often independently owned, but some major hotel chains have created unique boutique properties that show off the best of a particular city or neighborhood. What is the most luxurious hotel in Nashville? Every room in the pet-friendly hotel has live green plants, providing oxygen as you sleep. Where should I avoid staying in Nashville? Nashvilleâs core neighborhoods, including downtown, SoBro, and The Gulch, are quite walkable, but the further afield you go, the less you'll be able to walk, and public transportation options may become sparse. Budget hotels on and near Murfreesboro Pike are not close to many attractions, so any savings on room rates may be spent on parking and transportation. item.title: The best charity shops in London: a fashion editor's guide for secondhand gems
item.description:
Source: Condé Nast Traveler UK
In late 2019, I was hurrying home on a wintery afternoon down the Northcote Road in Battersea when my eyes were drawn to a suitcase in the window of the Royal Trinity Hospice charity shop. It wasn’t just any suitcase, it was an ivory, large check-in, two-wheeled trunk from luxury luggage makers Globetrotter, and it was in great condition. These retail for £2,495 in Burlington Arcade but in front of me the label read £100. What was the catch? “The keys are missing” the shopkeeper told me (nothing that an email to the company couldn’t fix), so five minutes later I was skipping back to Balham, suitcase flying behind me, happy in the knowledge I had donated to a charity that is dear to me. This is why I love charity shops: the thrill of looking for a steal and actually finding one. And the odds in London are in your favour, with over 800 stores in the city and many affluent and generous residents to donate. I love to mooch for crockery, glassware, books and jewellery. The trick is to know where to look and to have an open mind. Each London borough has a distinctive style, so don’t expect to find the same skirts in Chiswick as you'll find in Camden. The racks are rarely curated beyond ‘tops’ and ‘bottoms’ so be prepared to get stuck in. Charity shops offer a real opportunity to experiment with personal style, when prices are low and pieces don’t fit the current fashion trends, you can afford to get creative and crafty. We all know that trends are cyclical and chances are you might find some ultra trendy Noughties pieces that the Gen-Zers are picking up like hotcakes. Plus, secondhand shopping is a great way to give back not only to the named charity but to the environment – the fashion industry is one of the world's biggest polluters and we can all do our bit to help reduce our fashion footprint and increase the sustainability of our wardrobe. What’s better than a good old humble brag – “Oh, this old thing? I bought it from Oxfam”. With that in mind, here is my pick of the best charity shops in London for rack raiding: You know Traid is going to be a fun shopping experience before you cross the threshold, as the visual merchandising can only be described as exquisite. Curated by visual artist Francesco Colucci, the mannequins are dressed in his ‘ephemeral couture’ – a real manifestation of the creativity charity shops can foster. I particularly love the Brixton branch of Traid (which has 13 stores across London) because I know stylists shop there to source for photoshoots, and the local buzz of Brixton brings in some very fun and unique pieces. Traid also partners with Harrods on repair workshops, hosts styling sessions with fashion stylists and has a host of celebrity ambassadors who donate to store themselves, from Martin Freeman to Laura Bailey. Check their Instagram for their most exciting new drops, from of-the-moment Scandi brands to Wales Bonner tracksuits. I added this branch to my must-visit list after a charity shop crawl along Kensington High Street with a suavely dressed friend who swears by it. Incidentally that trip yielded a mint-condition Ferragamo silk scarf and an N.Peal cashmere crew neck sweater – I think they speak for themselves. It’s under-the-radar design means, despite its location, it's rarely busy and filled with hidden gems. Get there via an inspiring walk past the sharp dressers of Holland Park, or a quicker stroll from Kensington High Street station (past no less than four other leading London charity shops). Address: 266 Kensington High Street, London W8 6ND Website: octaviafoundation.org.uk/charity_shops I have to admit a personal bias toward this branch: it's my local and I regularly donate pieces from my own wardrobe. Across all 23 stores in central and south-west London, stock is kept fresh – director of retail Andy Keen has learnt this practice over the years. “We've know our customers really well. We know the kinds of pieces they love, and that can be different from one neighbourhood to the next. Most of our donations are sold close to where they were given, but we also move stock between shops when we think it will find the right home and to make sure there is always a changing selection in our shops.” Inside, everything is neatly organised by item type, sizing and colour palette, plus a dedicated rail for designer labels. A personal highlight is the accessories display, where I've even spotted rare pair Alexa Chung wedges up for grabs. Website: royaltrinityhospice.london/balham Mary's Living & Giving Shop for Save the Children, Primrose Hill The Primrose Hill branch, one of 17 of the elevated off-shoots from Save The Children set up with the Queen of Shops Mary Portas, feels like a high-end boutique. Outside there are two full height windows and inside the deep turquoise walls, wooden floors and pillared archways are warm and inviting. The staff make an effort to curate the rails for the season, with shearling coats in autumn and beach-ready buys in the summer. Particular specialities here are event dresses, designer shoes and really retro '90s designer shirts. The eclectic decor and trinkets are a visual feast and are reminiscent of that famous scene from Wild Child. Address: 109 Regent's Park Rd, London NW1 8UR An emporium of second hand clothes and bric-a-brac, the Fara in Islington is the largest of their 29 London branches (which include specialist book, kids and vintage stores). It is well known for being the place for cheap bargains. I love it here because it is understated and lauds the second life of unwanted items with the aim of us all living more sustainably. Only 5 minutes walk from Angel station it's very easy to get to and is conveniently sandwiched between two very nice pubs. Address: 28 Pentonville Road, London N1 9HJ If the Crisis shop Instagram is anything to go by, then you’re in for a treat. The page is poppy, contemporary and filled with hauls and styling tips from customers and exclusive collaborations with up and coming designers. There are 16 stores in London and a website where you can shop upcycled edits called ‘unsold retold’. Influencers are also invited to ‘Create for Crisis’ and the Dalston store Instagram posts events, such as ‘Dalstonbury.’ The focus here is on great high street buys, books, vinyl and small interior decorations. Address: 74 Kingsland High St, London E8 2NS Launched with fashion fan-fare in 2008 as the charity-shop sector's answer to musty clothes and worn-out shoes, the OG of curated second hand still stands proud with neighbours including Ganni and Sezane. The shop is a treasure trove of donations from the neighbourhood's generous patrons and stocks designer and premium labels for men and women. Add it to a day of second hand shopping including a mooch down neighbouring Portobello Road which is a veritable honeypot for second hand. There are only 3 of the boutiques in London, so it’s an easy bet that the good stuff (think Jimmy Choo, Missoni and Prada) will end up here. Address: 245 Westbourne Grove, London W11 2SE Car boot sales, in the yards of local schools, are picking up a cult following in London amongst fashionistas, students and second hand boutique buyers looking to find new stock. For a small fee visitors can find anything and everything on sale from tables and mirrors to boxes of homemade scrunchies and rails of vintage Burberry trenches. The Peckham Carboot organisers have opened a twin-sale in Balham and are looking to open new spots later this year in Stoke Newington and Leytonstone. Known at the Sunday Service and only open every other Sunday (and not in January) the carboot can get quite busy and vibey, with DJs and coffee vans. Importantly, and what earns them a place on this list, sellers who don’t shift all their wares at the sale are encouraged to donate them on site to sight loss charity Fight for Sight so no one goes home empty handed. Address: 112 Peckham Rd, London SE15 5DZ

item.title: 32 Serving Platters That Are As Centerpiece-Worthy As the Main Course

Iâm not going to argue that the manner in which a dish is plated and served actually affects the way it tastes (though I know some will). That said, Iâm of the belief that presentation does affect the experience of eating a meal. A simple roast chicken becomes that much more impressive when itâs carved neatly and arranged on a pretty scallop-edged platter, just as a plate of spaghetti pomodoro somehow becomes restaurant-worthy when the plate in question is a piece of hand-painted stoneware. Whether youâre looking to elevate your Sunday family suppers or deck out this year's holiday tablescape with a conversation-starting piece, these platters may just convince you to ditch your basic white serveware for something with a bit more personality. If your style leans minimalist and modern, these monochrome options will make an elegant addition to your serveware collection. Add a pop of color to the dinner table with a glossy glazed number, keep things neutral with a black marble tray, or go classic and Michelin-worthy with a Jono Pandolfi platter featuring the renowned ceramistâs signature exposed clay rim. For something more intricate, look to a hand-painted stoneware platter. Transport your dinner guests to Italy with a piece from the iconic Ginori 1735, or opt for something more graphic like a checkered platter from Maison FlÃ¢neur. A decorative edge is an elegant way to zhuzh up an otherwise plain platter, and it has the benefit of being visible even when that platter is full of food. Pretty ruffles, bead-like dots, or orderly scallops? Take your pick. I wouldnât recommend using most of the above for any outdoor entertainingâitâs not worth the risk of turning your gorgeous new hand-painted stoneware into a pile of shards. Instead, opt for a lightweight shatterproof material like enamelware, melamine, or wood to serve this summerâs helpings of grilled kebabs and sliced watermelon. Iâm particularly fond of the glossy serveware from UK-based brand Falcon Enamelware, and I was delighted to find out that contrary to what Iâd always been told about enamelware, Falconâs products are all dishwasher-safe.
